title: Filing Your Return
description: Who files, when the money is due, and how a mistake gets fixed.
wolfLine: The extension moves the form. It does not move the payment.

filing-extension.definition: Extra time to send the return, usually to October 15. It does not give extra time to pay the tax.
filing-extension.example: An extension filed on April 15 still leaves an $800 tax due on April 15.

amended-return.definition: A form, usually Form 1040-X, that fixes a return you already filed. You generally have about three years, and the exact deadline is on irs.gov for that year.
amended-return.example: A missed $200 credit is fixed on an amended return, not by filing the original form again and hoping.

lessons.title: Who Must File
lessons.summary: The common cases, not every exception.

steps.title: Usually, not always
steps.body:
You usually must file if your income is above the filing threshold for your status, and if you had at least **$400** of net self-employment income. That $400 rule is the common case.

You may still want to file when you do not have to, so a refund or a refundable credit can reach you. This is the usual rule, not a ruling on your year.

steps.prompt: Who usually must file even with a small income?
choices: Someone with $400 or more of net self-employment income
Someone with no income and no credits
Someone whose only mail was a grocery flyer
steps.explain: Self-employment of $400 or more is a common filing trigger.

steps.prompt: If a refund is waiting, filing can still be worth it when you are not required to file.
steps.explain: The IRS does not mail the refund just because it would have been nice.

steps.prompt: What is the careful way to know if you must file this year?
choices: Check the filing threshold for your status on irs.gov
File only if you owe more than $1,000
steps.explain: Thresholds depend on age, status, and the year. The IRS page is the list.

steps.prompt: Net self-employment of $___ or more usually means you must file.
steps.explain: The common figure is $400 of net self-employment income.

lessons.title: Deadlines and Extensions
lessons.summary: More time to file is not more time to pay.

steps.title: April, then October
steps.body:
A calendar-year return is usually due **April 15**. If that day is a weekend or a holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

A [[filing extension]] usually gives you until **October 15** to send the form. The tax is still due in April. An **$800** tax unpaid from April 15 to October 15 is six months late even if the form is on time.

steps.prompt: What does an extension extend?
choices: The time to file the return
The time to pay the tax
The time to earn the income
steps.explain: File later. Pay on time.

steps.prompt: The tax due on April 15 is $800. An extension is filed and the return is sent on October 15. How much of that tax was still due in April?
steps.explain: All $800. The extension did not move the payment.

steps.prompt: April 15 to October 15 is how many months?
steps.explain: October 15 is six months after April 15.

steps.prompt: A return filed on October 15, under an extension, was required to include the payment back in April.
steps.explain: The form may be on time in October. The payment was due in April.

lessons.title: What to Gather
lessons.summary: The return is only as good as the stack.

steps.title: The usual pile
steps.body:
Bring the [[W-2|w-2]] from each job, any [[1099|form-1099]], and the records of a credit you will claim. A grocery receipt is not a tax form.

Last year’s return helps you type the numbers. It does not replace this year’s W-2.

steps.prompt: Sort the pile.
items: A grocery receipt for ordinary food
steps.explain: Income forms come in. Ordinary groceries and greeting cards do not.

steps.prompt: You had two jobs. How many W-2s do you need?
choices: Neither, if you remember the pay
steps.explain: Each employer reports its own wages and withholding.

steps.prompt: A grocery receipt belongs in the tax pile for a person who did not itemize and did not run a business.
steps.explain: Ordinary food is not a line on that return.

steps.prompt: Bank interest arrives on a Form ___.
steps.explain: 1099-INT. The W-4 is the withholding form, not the interest form.

lessons.title: Filing Status
lessons.summary: It picks the deduction and the brackets.

steps.title: Five names
steps.body:
The common statuses are single, married filing jointly, married filing separately, head of household, and qualifying surviving spouse.

Head of household is not “I own a house.” It is usually an unmarried person who paid for a home for a qualifying person. The 2026 standard deduction you already saw is **$16,100** single and **$24,150** head of household.

steps.prompt: Two spouses can choose which pair?
choices: Married filing jointly or married filing separately
Single and head of household, both at once
A status from a different year
steps.explain: Spouses pick joint or separate. They do not each file as single.

steps.prompt: Owning a house, by itself, makes you head of household.
steps.explain: The status is about a qualifying person and paying for the home, not about the mortgage.

steps.prompt: How much larger is the 2026 head-of-household standard deduction than the single one?
Spouses who file together use married filing ___.
steps.explain: Jointly is the shared return. Separately is the other choice.

lessons.title: Free Help or a Preparer
lessons.summary: The fee is not the same thing as a correct return.

steps.title: Three doors
steps.body:
IRS Free File and VITA can cost nothing if you qualify. Paid software and a preparer charge a fee. This page does not grade an income cap, because those caps change. Check irs.gov for the year.

Whoever prepares it, you sign it. The **$350** fee does not move the tax rules.

lines.label: Software fee on this Free File offer

docs.note: A $0 fee only if you qualify. Check irs.gov.

steps.prompt: You qualify for Free File and your return is the single-filer case from this course. Which page has the lower fee?
why: The offer on this page is $0 if you qualify.
steps.explain: Qualify first. If you do, the fee on this pair is $0 versus $350.

steps.prompt: A preparer’s signature replaces yours.
steps.explain: You sign your return. The preparer can be wrong, and the return is still yours.

steps.prompt: VITA and Free File are the right first look when what is true?
choices: You might qualify for free help
You want a fee in every case
You would rather skip the W-2
steps.explain: Check the qualification. Then decide if a fee buys you something the free option does not.

lessons.title: A Simplified Form 1040
lessons.summary: Five lines. The refund is not one of the wages.

steps.title: The story you already know
steps.body:
This is the single filer with **$40,000** of wages, the 2026 [[standard deduction]] of **$16,100**, tax of **$2,620**, and withholding of **$3,000**.

The lines are different kinds of numbers. Do not add the wages to the tax.

doc.title: A simplified Form 1040
doc.subtitle: Single, 2026
doc.note: Taxable income is wages minus the $16,100 standard deduction. The lines are not one total.

steps.prompt: What is taxable income on this form?

doc.title: A simplified Form 1040
doc.subtitle: Single, 2026
doc.note: Taxable income is wages minus the $16,100 standard deduction. The lines are not one total.

steps.prompt: What is the refund?
Which line is the prepayment?
steps.explain: Withholding is what was already sent. Wages are what you earned.

steps.prompt: Adding all five lines gives a number the IRS uses.
steps.explain: They are not the same kind of dollar. The refund is withholding minus tax.

lessons.title: E-file and Direct Deposit
lessons.summary: The refund goes where the numbers say.

steps.title: Type the account twice
steps.body:
E-file sends the return electronically. Direct deposit sends a refund to the routing number and account number you enter.

A refund of **$380** deposited to the right account is $380. The same refund sent to a wrong account is a problem you have to unwind. Paper checks are slower.

steps.prompt: What does direct deposit need?
choices: The right routing number and account number
A paper check from last year
steps.explain: Those two numbers are the address of the account.

steps.prompt: The refund is $380 and the preparer fee was $0. How much of the refund is left after a $0 fee?
steps.explain: $380 − $0 = $380. A fee would come out of your pocket, not out of the tax math.

steps.prompt: E-file means you no longer need the W-2.
steps.explain: E-file is how the return travels. The W-2 is still the source of the wages and the withholding.

steps.prompt: A wrong account number can send the refund to the wrong ___.
steps.explain: Check the digits before you submit.

lessons.title: Denise Fixes a Mistake
lessons.summary: An extension paid on time. A credit fixed later.

story.title: Denise fixes a return
story.body:
Denise is 41 and a clinic manager. She filed an extension and paid her **$800** tax on April 15, then sent the return in June. The payment was on time. The form used the extra time.

In August she finds a **$200** credit the return left off. She files an [[amended return]], usually Form 1040-X. She does not file the original form a second time.

The credit would have cut her tax from **$800** to **$600**. She checks irs.gov for how long an amended return for that year is allowed. The usual window is about three years.

steps.prompt: Denise’s original tax was $800. The missed credit is $200. What should the tax have been?
How much did she overpay if she already paid the $800?
How does she fix the filed return?
choices: A second copy of the original return
A new W-4 sent to the IRS
steps.explain: The amended return is the correction. A second original is not.

steps.prompt: Her extension let her pay the $800 in October.
steps.explain: She paid in April. The extension covered the form, not the payment.

steps.prompt: The form that usually fixes a filed return is Form ___.
steps.explain: 1040-X. Then check the deadline for that year on irs.gov.

lessons.title: Sharpen Up
lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Filing Your Return
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: An extension to file is also an extension to pay.
steps.explain: The return can wait until October. The tax is still due in April.

steps.prompt: Which paper reports wages and federal income tax withheld?
steps.explain: The W-2 is the wage report. The W-4 is the withholding request.

steps.prompt: A return left off a $150 credit. The tax paid was $900. What should the tax have been?
You qualify for free help. What is the first door?
choices: The most expensive preparer in town
steps.explain: Check that you qualify, then use the free door before you pay $350.
